Use historically plausible Roman military architecture and do not add unsupported monumental fantasy decoration.
contextual: Construction progress, workers, legionary activity, camera distance, weather, and time-of-day may change with the scene.

anchors.name: Legio IX Hispana Military Kit and Standard Continuity
anchors.rationale: Several reconstruction scenes depict the same legion across marching, construction, battle-hypothesis, and summary beats; its equipment language must remain coherent without inventing unsupported Ninth Legion heraldry.

locked: Keep one plausible early-second-century Roman legionary equipment family across helmets, armor, shields, belts, clothing, packs, and standards.
Maintain consistent material age, construction quality, and military status cues across recurring reconstruction scenes.
Do not assign a unique emblem, shield device, animal symbol, color scheme, or heraldic mark specifically to Legio IX unless an approved source supports it.
A standard may communicate Roman military identity, but unsupported decorative detail must remain generic and non-assertive.
contextual: Individual soldiers may vary naturally in face, pose, age, weather exposure, and minor equipment state.
Marching, construction work, and hypothetical battle may change loadout and posture while retaining the same equipment design family.
